messages.subject: Re: Completed summary ready for your arithmetic review
messages.body:
Gate-by-gate verification complete. Every number in your summary reproduces exactly and every gate holds. engineering_accepted=true is supported. Source-only, no reruns.

GOVERNING TEXT. I verified against acceptance-v2/PROMOTION_RULE.md (50 lines, sha256 0fa83c9fd5b7aec789c6a53757f0cefd10180c46e704190192590ec16075bae2 as recorded in pins.json), not the 36-line acceptance/ copy. The v2 file is the acceptance/ text plus a 14-line appended section adding power preconditions, caffeinate and the at-least-60-minute window. I checked that appended section separately; results below. Both copies hash to their recorded values.

ARITHMETIC. All 16 scenario medians recompute as the mean of sorted ranks 3 and 4 and match to the last digit. All four percent changes are ratio of medians, median(candidate)/median(baseline), not median of within-pair ratios: initial +0.444331, noop -2.468462, body -1.381043, structural -0.287185. All 24 paired percent changes reproduce exactly under repeat-index pairing. mean_scenario_median_ratio 0.990769102733662 exact. Sum of medians 22.157860001025 to 22.085534146114 seconds, -0.072325854911 s, -0.326411733 percent, exact.

SIX PERFORMANCE GATES, with margins so the narrowness is on record.
1. Noop ratio of medians 0.975315381773 at or below 0.98: PASS. The candidate needed 2.075093242 s and delivered 2.065173834 s, 9.92 ms of headroom, 0.47 pp.
2. All six paired noop ratios below 1: PASS. Worst is pair 1 at 0.998371242683, a 3.41 ms margin on a 2.096 s measurement.
3. Initial, body, structural median regressions at or below 2 percent: PASS at +0.444331, -1.381043, -0.287185.
4. Every scenario median RSS increase at or below 5 percent: PASS at +0.555573, -7.123887, +1.858094, -1.381228. Noop 382.406 to 355.164 MiB confirmed.
5. Mean scenario median ratio below 1: PASS at 0.990769.
6. Sum of median scenario times nonincreasing: PASS at -72.3 ms. Decomposition: initial costs +51.0 ms, noop returns -52.3 ms, body -58.8 ms, structural -12.3 ms.

On the initial regression I applied the sum-nonincreasing bound rather than the nominal 2 percent, as I said I would. The two-scenario bound I derived before data was Y at most 0.184825 times X, which for this cohort permits initial +0.456233 percent; realized is +0.444331 percent. So noop alone pays for the initial regression by 1.2 ms. Body supplies the actual slack. The binding constraint here was never the 2 percent line.

CORRECTNESS, recomputed rather than read off your flags. Cross-arm graph hashes: exactly one distinct value per label across all twelve arms, 7fe9440b1d16a8d3 for initial/noop/body/cold-original/cold-body and 5dec281283083790 for structural/cold-structural, with wire.normalized_hash equal to graph_hash wherever published. Within every arm, incremental equals cold for initial, body and structural: zero mismatches in 36 comparisons. Noop in all twelve arms: state_before equals state_after, zero wire messages, BaseGeneration 1 to TargetGeneration 1, zero parsed and zero read. Broker: completeness_status success and batch_count_matches_end true for all twelve arms on every published label; noop correctly has neither. All twelve arms exit 0, no errors, all_checks_validated true, timing_eligible true, correctness_only false, no background or host sample errors. Twelve runs, no thirteenth arm directory, so no refill.

COUNTERBALANCING. Realized order is B1,C1,C2,B2,B3,C3,C4,B4,B5,C5,C6,B6, which is AB,BA,AB,BA,AB,BA: three of each as the rule requires, all twelve inside one window.

HOST CONDITIONS. Pressure: 3610 samples across twelve files, every one Darwin dispatch level 1, maximum gap 0.2692 s, so the 250 ms cadence held and nothing approached the one-second rejection threshold. Swapouts constant at 3042366 across all 24 observations, so zero new Swapouts; Swapins rise monotonically 2149325 to 2155347 in arm order with no resets, reported as context only. Wall minus monotonic drift is at most 4.9 ms per arm, so no suspension anywhere: the failure mode that ended the previous attempt did not recur. Host audit 31 samples per arm, no errors, maximum sample gaps 2.13 to 2.17 s.

THE APPENDED POWER SECTION. AC power at all 24 boundary observations. Charge 63 to 81 percent, rising monotonically, every observation at or above the 20 percent floor. lowpowermode 0 in the AC profile before and after every arm. All twelve power observations bracket their arm's monotonic interval. summarize-timing.py line 52 recomputes require_power_evidence and raises on mismatch, which satisfies the "independently validate it in the final summarizer" clause fail-closed; power_gate.py also retains rejected observations rather than dropping them, matching "missing or failed observations reject the cohort". caffeinate appears in 31 of 31 whole-host samples in every one of the twelve arms, 372 of 372. One precision: the sampler omits process arguments, so the -i flag specifically is not verifiable from the receipts; what is verifiable is that caffeinate ran throughout every arm and that no sleep occurred. I am not treating the boundary power checks as proof of uninterrupted AC within an arm, consistent with your own wording in the rule and in power_gate's coverage annotation.

WINDOW AND PINS. All twelve arms ran 13:20:02 to 13:35:48 UTC, entirely inside the granted 13:20:00 to 14:25:00, using 15.76 of 65 minutes; the appended at-least-60-minute planning requirement was honored in the request even though the cohort finished far inside it. timing_gate.py in current-roster mode checks each participant's own message id and from_handle against its own body and evidence hash, which is the property I asked for: my ACK cannot stand in for another participant's. I verified by hashing that both binaries, the pinned rule copy, cli.py, the scope yaml and the full-suite receipt match their recorded sha256s, and that both arms use byte-identical argv except --binary, with ENOLA_GRAPH_PROFILE popped, so no scratch profiling instrumentation was active.

FINDINGS TO RECORD IN THE ARCHIVE. None of these is a gate failure.

1. payload_bytes_total differs deterministically: +3092 initial, +3 body, +4 structural. Fully explained, zero unexplained bytes. It localizes to begin +2, end +1, batches +3089 on initial, which is exactly 1.0 byte per batch. The cause is the run identifier length: 59 chars for the candidate against 58 for the baseline, because "candidate" is nine characters and "baseline" is eight. One byte times 3091 messages plus one more because the begin message carries the identifier twice gives +3092 exactly; structural 3+1 gives +4 and body 2+1 gives +3. All three match to the byte. This is a harness naming artifact, not candidate behavior. Worth recording so the delta is not later mistaken for a publication-content change. The rule has no payload-bytes condition and messages_observed, node and edge records, graph totals and deltas, owner_scope_count, schema_version, scope_mode and generation_kind are all identical.

2. state_final_bytes varies run to run within the same binary: baseline 90686486 to 90686597, candidate 90686492 to 90686818. So "unchanged checkpoint bytes" is satisfiable only as the within-noop before/after invariant, which holds in all twelve arms, and can never be read as cross-arm byte identity. Consistent with the standing rule that digests are not byte equality.

3. summary_scans and derived_indexes are nondeterministic in both arms with heavily overlapping ranges, and the candidate medians move -3.5 and +3.5. The two counters that plausibly track the two named mechanisms therefore neither corroborate nor contradict them. The accepted claim should stay "the combined new changes", which is what the rule already says. I did not normalize these fields away.

4. Position effect, the most interesting new observation. AB and BA group means differ materially: noop -1.6669 against -3.2419 percent, a 1.5750 pp gap; body -0.0621 against -1.4309, 1.3688 pp; structural +0.5578 against -2.4073, 2.9652 pp; initial -0.6091 against +1.1360, 1.7451 pp and opposite in sign. In noop, body and structural the second-position arm of a pair is the slower one. At three pairs per group this is descriptive, not established. The point is that its magnitude is comparable to the treatment effect and much larger than pair 1's 0.163 pp margin, so counterbalancing is doing real work here and six-of-six survived by less than the apparent position effect. This is an observation about design sensitivity, not a request to change anything.

5. Sensitivity note on initial, stated as a note only. The initial comparison is +0.444331 percent over six pairs; dropping pair 4, whose +3.88 percent is the cohort's outlier, would give -0.4388 percent. The sign of the initial figure is therefore not robust at this spread, which licenses neither a regression claim nor an improvement claim. I am not proposing any rule variant and not asking for a subset analysis; the six-pair figure stands as computed.

6. Competing load, reported honestly rather than as a clean bill. Sum of the top-twelve listed foreign CPU means averages 84.47 percent during baseline arms, range 80.64 to 89.69, and 83.70 percent during candidate arms, range 81.17 to 86.45. That 0.77 pp is a direction favoring the candidate, small against a 2.47 percent noop effect, and per pair it does not track the results: pair 1, the smallest noop win, had candidate load 2.70 pp higher, and pair 4, the +3.88 percent initial outlier, had candidate load 8.28 pp lower. So recorded competitor CPU does not explain the initial outlier. That outlier stays unexplained rather than attributed.

TWO ARCHIVE-HYGIENE ITEMS.
a. full-suite-receipt.json records command "go test ./..." with exit 0 and elapsed 150.745 s, but no -count=1 and no start or end wall timestamps, so the receipt by itself cannot exclude cached package results. 150.7 s is consistent with real execution; the receipt just cannot distinguish. Your call whether that matters for the archive; I am not asking for a rerun.
b. pins.json still carries purpose "Prospective summary-noop acceptance; no samples yet", which is now stale. Also worth one line in the archive: pair-receipt.json records a single quiet_ack_message_id, mine, which must not be read as the window authorization. The four-participant roster in timing-window.json, validated per participant by timing_gate.py, is the authorization. I cannot and did not speak for the other three.

SCOPE LIMITS, restating the rule's own closing paragraph so publication does not overreach: this is a limited engineering promotion gate, not statistical significance, not near-zero fresh-noop completion, not resident-watch latency, not old-upstream comparison, and not complete current-main historical coverage. The six pairs are descriptive. Those obligations remain open.

One boundary I am keeping explicit: absolute seconds from this cohort must not be compared against Stage32 or the rejected attempt, because per-arm host speed has varied about threefold across sessions and that variation is still unexplained. Every gate here is a ratio or a within-cohort comparison, which is why a host-speed factor largely cancels; what a slow or noisy host threatens is per-pair spread, so the realistic risk was rejection on consistency, not false acceptance.

Nothing under /tmp/enola-summary-noop/ was modified; I read only. I did not edit the pinned rule to record the granted interval, as previously agreed; the window belongs in the result files. The timing hold is released and I am idle and source-only. Standing offer continues for any future cohort: I will verify the computed summary gate by gate against the frozen text, including the conditions that pass.

messages.subject: Re: Review scope reminder after compaction
messages.body:
Acknowledged, and the verification you are waiting on is already sent: msg_56076d209e88, replying to msg_cf446385f996. It is the full gate-by-gate pass over acceptance-v2/timing-comparison.json against acceptance-v2/PROMOTION_RULE.md. Short form: every figure in your summary reproduces exactly, all six performance gates pass, correctness/broker/cross-arm-hash/pressure/swap/power/window/pin conditions all hold, and engineering_accepted=true is supported. Publish when ready from my side.

Scope confirmed: runtime 3f2883b Stage33 only. I reviewed nothing else, requested nothing else, and treat every prior stage and prototype review as closed. Existing summary reports accepted as reported. The new diagnostic profile docs are separate from runtime and from this acceptance data; I did not read them into this verification.

Three things worth having in front of you before publication, all detailed in msg_56076d209e88 and none of them a gate failure. The margins are narrow and should be published as such: 9.92 ms of headroom on the noop ratio and 3.41 ms on the worst paired noop ratio. The deterministic payload_bytes_total deltas of +3092, +4 and +3 are fully explained by the one-character difference between the baseline and candidate run identifiers and are a harness naming artifact, so they should be labeled that way in the archive rather than left to look like a publication-content change. And two hygiene items: full-suite-receipt.json records go test ./... without -count=1 and without wall timestamps, so it cannot by itself exclude cached package results, and cli-pairs/pins.json still says "Prospective summary-noop acceptance; no samples yet".

On the archive: docs/benchmarks/watch-fanout-2026-09-26/summary-noop/timing-accepted-20260927 is not present in my checkout at 674cf84, so I have verified the acceptance-v2 scratch tree and not the archived copy. That is a limit of my view, not a claim about your worktree. If you want the archived copy checked for consistency against the scratch numbers before publication, point me at a path I can read and I will diff the medians, the paired arrays and the decision block; source-only, no reruns.

No hold needed, nothing running on my side, idle and source-only.
